clue.text: Unnamed pet fed by book group

indicators.note: something fed takes food inside it

parts.note: canoodle = to pet, cuddle; drop N (name)
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A nameless pet is being fed by a group reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is the verb here: to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle. It hides behind the picture of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle survives almost only in the idiom 'the whole caboodle', meaning the whole lot or group.

clue.text: Half-capsized vessels tip

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, and 'half' limits that to one half of the word, the back half here

parts.note: cups are drinking vessels; its second half PS turns to SP

explanation.surface: Boats have half-capsized and are tipping over.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessels look like boats but are cups, which is what makes 'capsized' so natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is the pointed end where two curves meet, as on a tooth or the horns of a crescent moon.

clue.text: Total enthusiast supporting British game and veg

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever supports another word sits beneath it, holding it up

parts.note: B is short for British
utter = total, as in utter nonsense
a nut = a fan, as in golf nut
squash is a racket game

explanation.surface: A total fan of a British sport who also likes vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total enthusiast' reads as one phrase and is one, an utter nut, placed below the British.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut squash is a pear-shaped orange-fleshed squash, a specific example of veg.

clue.text: Fine house under protection of Buddhist state

parts.note: OK = fine

indicators.note: something under another's protection is sheltered within it, so the house sits inside the Buddhist

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A fine house enjoys the protection of a Buddhist state such as Tibet or Bhutan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddhist state' reads as one idea, but the state is the definition on its own and the Buddhist is a lama.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Oklahoma is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Beaten sailor conceding nothing retreats

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are, so the letters are whisked into a new order
conceding means giving up a letter, taken out of the sailor word before mixing

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round symbol for nothing

explanation.surface: A defeated seaman, admitting nothing, withdraws.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairs are dens where animals hide, places of refuge one retreats to.

clue.text: Agency's order returned work in pieces

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the CIA's, the US intelligence agency
OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An agency sends back an order for a job that arrived in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work in pieces' sounds like a botched job but describes the artwork exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a work of art built from small pieces of tile or glass, so the definition is a cryptic description.

clue.text: Annoyed after raising available yield

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a part lifts it to the top, so the phrase is read after that part has been moved up

parts.note: out = available, as a book newly out
annoyed = PUT OUT; its OUT is lifted above PUT

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at having to raise the available yield.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the part to move: of PUT OUT, the 'available' part is the one raised to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Output and yield are plain synonyms for the amount something produces, as in a farm's or factory's yield.

clue.text: Line-up at ten excited couple third from the end

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: A queue forming at ten o'clock gets an excited pair third from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges LINEUPATTEN into ANTEPENULTI, then MATE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Antepenultimate means before the penultimate, that is coming third from last in a series.

clue.text: Chip in centre of tabula: sorry about that

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, here the two middle letters of a six-letter word
about in the sense of around, so the sorry word surrounds the centre

parts.note: contrite = sorry, penitent
the middle two letters of TABULA

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for putting a chip in the middle of a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry about that' reads as an apology tacked on at the end; 'about' is doing the work of a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an informal idiom for putting money or effort into a shared pot.

clue.text: Rejection of the other new American bicycle

indicators.note: a new version of something has been remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: A is short for American
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a new American bike for the other one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British slang for sex, so rejecting it is celibacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibacy is abstaining from sex, which coy British slang calls 'a bit of the other'.

clue.text: Object launched from rocky islet late

indicators.note: rocky also means unsteady, and letters on unsteady ground wobble into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Something launched late from a rocky little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky islet' reads as scenery, but 'rocky' is what shakes the letters up.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial satellite is sent up by rocket, so an object launched describes it well.

clue.text: Huge giants essentially tracking bird

definitions.note: the noun used attributively, as in a titan of a man; it stands for something huge

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the middle letters come after the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the middle letters of giants

parts.note: middle letters taken

explanation.surface: Huge giants at heart, following a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Huge giants' reads as one phrase, but 'giants' is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Titan was one of the colossal gods of Greek myth, so the word stands for anything of immense size.

clue.text: Coach abandoning first-class college

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so the coach word leaves its A out

parts.note: to coach = to teach
A = first-class, top grade; removed

explanation.surface: A coach walks out on a top college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer or a bus; it is the verb, teach.
explanation.definitionFit: Tech is the British short form for a technical college, where vocational subjects are taught.

clue.text: Omit scrubbing soft garment one takes off

indicators.note: to scrub a plan is to cancel it, so the soft letter is cancelled from the word

parts.note: to skip = to omit
p = piano, soft in music; scrubbed from SKIP
a jumper is a British word for a sweater

explanation.surface: Skip washing the soft jumper someone takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' suggests removing a garment, which the jumper encourages; the ski jumper takes off from the ramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jumper launches from the end of a ramp, so 'one takes off' is a cryptic description of the flight.

clue.text: Ignoring borders, wimpy pilots over time defect

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the pieces before sit above the time letter
the borders of a word are its outer letters, ignored here

parts.note: inner letters taken
airmen are pilots

explanation.surface: Weedy pilots, over time, desert across the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defect' looks like a verb about deserting, but it is a noun meaning flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: An impairment is a weakness or damage that reduces function, a flaw in something.

clue.text: Obsessive national hiding number in coat

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the national holds the number within

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat

indicators.note: placed in, so the whole assembly goes inside the coat

parts.note: someone from Oman
No. is short for number

explanation.surface: An obsessive foreigner hides a number inside his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a nest of two containers, so the smallest one is built first and the coat wraps it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A monomaniac is fixated on a single subject, so obsessive works as a noun: an obsessive person.

clue.text: Iris scan arranged for poet's host?

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in order, as with flowers, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Irises and other flowers arranged for a poet's host.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth saw 'a host, of golden daffodils', and daffodils are narcissi; the question mark flags that allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils belong to the genus Narcissus, so Wordsworth's host of golden daffodils was a host of narcissi.

clue.text: Slight man finally saved by vessel

indicators.note: saved by means the letter is held safe inside the vessel word

parts.note: a sub, a submarine, is a vessel

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of man

parts.note: last letter taken

explanation.surface: A man is rescued by a ship at the last moment, if only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' is a noun or verb meaning an insult, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a deliberate insult, the same as a slight or cold shoulder.

clue.text: African petition blocked by Europeans

indicators.note: a pipe blocked by something has it lodged inside, so the Europeans sit inside the petition

parts.note: to sue = to petition, appeal
Danes are from Denmark

explanation.surface: An African's petition is blocked by European officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Europeans' tempts a solver to write E for European; here it is a whole nation, the Danes.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: a Sudanese person, from Sudan, is one kind of African.

clue.text: Portion of oatcakes rolled in minutes

indicators.note: something rolled over ends up the other way round, so the piece reads backwards
a portion is a piece of the whole, so the answer is a piece of the word

parts.note: oATCAkes

explanation.surface: A piece of oatcake is rolled in a coating for a few minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' looks like time; it is the written record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is the Latin word used for official records of proceedings, the same sense as a meeting's minutes.

clue.text: Swimmer welcome around Yankee isle

indicators.note: around means the welcome word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Mull is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A swimmer gets a welcome around an American island.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey mullet is a fish of coastal waters, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: End up consuming second small Manhattan cocktail

indicators.note: consuming means the reversed word swallows the other letters
up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
mo is a short moment, a second

explanation.surface: Finish up by downing a second small cocktail in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan' goes with the definition: Americans call this drink a mimosa, the British a Buck's Fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimosa is champagne mixed with orange juice, the American name for that brunch drink.

clue.text: Mass shortened to accommodate model is essential

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to make room inside, so the model goes within the Mass
'shortened' cuts a letter off

parts.note: REQUIEM, a Mass for the dead, less M
to sit = to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A church service is cut short to make room for a model, and that is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mass is a specific one, the Requiem, and the model is a verb, what a person does for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Requisite, from Latin requirere, is a plain synonym for essential or necessary.

clue.text: English mutt spitting out one round date

indicators.note: spitting out means ejecting, so one round letter leaves the word for mutt

parts.note: a pooch is a dog, a mutt
a round thing is O, and only one of the two goes

explanation.surface: An English dog spitting out a ball, perhaps on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: POOCH loses one of its two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period of time marked by distinctive events, like a date in history.

clue.text: Greedy performer making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, and a return runs back the way it came, so read the word backwards

parts.note: a diva is a star singer

explanation.surface: A greedy star stages a comeback tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's comeback tour is exactly what a diva does, which hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid comes from Latin avidus, greedy, and keeps that sense in 'avid for money'.

clue.text: Female group putting green car into empty bay

indicators.note: putting the car into the bay signals placing letters inside
putting into means the car letters go inside the emptied bay
an empty word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters taken
an EV, electric vehicle, is a green car

explanation.surface: A group of women parks an eco-friendly car in a vacant bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, the collective noun traditionally used for women or for quails.

clue.text: Zeus's daughter joining Demeter at Olympus

indicators.note: the answer lies where the words join, spanning the gaps between them

parts.note: demetER AT Olympus

explanation.surface: A daughter of Zeus joins the goddess Demeter on Mount Olympus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is entirely Greek myth, and the answer belongs in that scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato, muse of love poetry, is one of the nine Muses, all daughters of Zeus.

clue.text: Fired items in stock to cover different area

indicators.note: to cover means the stock word goes over the other letters

parts.note: goods in stock are in store, so this gives the stock word store
new means different, as in a new look

explanation.surface: Kiln-fired pots held in stock cover a different area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacked, but it is baking in a kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is pottery fired at high temperatures in a kiln until dense and hard.

clue.text: Capital tense with what was published

parts.note: T is short for tense in grammar
eh? = what?
a story ran = it was printed

explanation.surface: A capital city is on edge about what has been published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective, nervous; it gives the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: One in article really taking things wrongly

indicators.note: one placed in the article sits inside it

parts.note: the definite article
I = one
very = really

explanation.surface: Someone in a newspaper article really misreads things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking things wrongly' suggests misunderstanding; it means stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a cryptic paraphrase: thievery is taking what belongs to others, taking it wrongfully.
